translations.literal: Namuzhal sent Ailong'a back ahead on the road, while he with San Tai and Kuimadai led two hundred horsemen forward by night, encountered more than three thousand rebels, were surrounded in many rings, fought until arrows were exhausted, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Namuzhal sent Ailong'a ahead; he, San Tai, and Kuimadai pushed two hundred horsemen forward by night, met three thousand rebels, fought until arrows ran out, and died.

sentences.zh: 上聞，追封三等義烈公，諡武毅。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard he posthumously enfeoffed him as third-class Duke Yilie with the posthumous title Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor posthumously made him third-class Duke Yilie with posthumous title Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He was enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 回部平，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When the Muslim regions were pacified his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Muslim regions were pacified his portrait joined the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 子保寧，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Baoning has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoning has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 保泰，自拜唐阿累遷察哈爾都統，與雅滿泰同為駐藏大臣，廓爾喀侵藏，保泰坐請達賴喇嘛、班禪額爾德尼避兵，又匿廓爾喀未構兵前表貢方物，及遣使有所請不以入奏，上改其名曰俘習渾，與雅滿泰同奪職荷校，先後予杖者四。

translations.literal: Baotai, rising from baitangga through successive promotions to Chahar commander-in-chief, served with Yamantai as resident commissioner in Tibet; when Nepal invaded Tibet, Baotai was punished for asking the Dalai Lama and Panchen Erdeni to avoid battle, and also for concealing Nepal's tribute goods sent before hostilities and envoys' requests without memorializing— the Emperor changed his name to Fuxihun; he and Yamantai were both stripped of office and made to wear the cangue; each was flogged four times in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Baotai rose to Chahar commander and served in Tibet with Yamantai; during the Gurkha invasion he was punished for urging the Dalai Lama and Panchen to flee, concealing prewar tribute, and failing to report Nepalese demands—the Emperor renamed him Fuxihun; he and Yamantai lost office, wore the cangue, and were flogged four times each.

sentences.zh: 藏事定，戍俘習渾黑龍江。

translations.literal: When Tibetan affairs were settled Fuxihun was banished to Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Tibet was settled Fuxihun was exiled to Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 赦還。

translations.literal: He was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was later pardoned and returned.

sentences.zh: 雅滿泰复授侍衛。

translations.literal: Yamantai was again appointed a guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: Yamantai was restored as a guardsman.

sentences.zh: 三泰，石氏，漢​​軍正白旗人，都統石文炳孫也。

translations.literal: San Tai, of the Shi clan, was a Chinese Martial of the Plain White Banner, grandson of Commander-in-chief Shi Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: San Tai of the Shi clan, Plain White Chinese Martial Banner, was Commander Shi Wenbing's grandson.

sentences.zh: 父觀音保，官至都統。

translations.literal: His father Guanyinbao rose to commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guanyinbao became commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三泰，自藍翎侍衛累遷正紅旗漢軍副都統、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: San Tai, from blue-plume guardsman, was promoted in succession to deputy commander of the Plain Red Banner of the Chinese Martial and Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: San Tai rose from blue-plume guardsman to Plain Red Chinese Martial deputy commander and Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十三年，命軍機處行走，調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Qianlong he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council and was shifted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 23 he entered the Grand Council and became Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 命以參贊大臣行走從納穆札爾出西路。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as coordinating commissioner and follow Namuzhal on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent as coordinating commissioner on the western route with Namuzhal.

sentences.zh: 七月，命納穆札爾、三泰率健銳營及索倫、察哈爾兵應兆惠。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Namuzhal and San Tai were ordered to lead the Vanguard Camp and Solon and Chahar troops to support Zhaohui.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he and Namuzhal led Vanguard, Solon, and Chahar troops to relieve Zhaohui.

sentences.zh: 夜進，期以黎明至兆惠軍。

translations.literal: They advanced by night, expecting to reach Zhaohui's army at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: They marched by night, expecting to reach Zhaohui at dawn.

sentences.zh: 遇賊，眾寡勢不敵，力戰，三泰墜馬，徒步擊賊，中創死。

translations.literal: They met rebels; force and numbers were unequal; fighting hard, San Tai fell from his horse, fought on foot, was wounded, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, they fought hard; San Tai fell from his horse, fought on foot, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 三等侍衛彰武、藍翎侍衛班泰、管站四品花翎西拉布、護軍校委署章京齊旺扎布及兆惠所遣迎師三等侍衛奎瑪岱，皆死。

translations.literal: Third-rank guardsman Zhangwu, blue-plume guardsman Bantai, fourth-rank station chief Xilabu with peacock feather, guards officer Qi Wang Zhab, and third-rank guardsman Kuimadai sent by Zhaohui to meet the army—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwu, Bantai, Xilabu, Qi Wang Zhab, and Kuimadai all died with them.

sentences.zh: 上聞，追封三等子，諡果勇。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard he posthumously enfeoffed him as third-class viscount with the posthumous title Guoyong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor posthumously made him third-class viscount Guoyong.

sentences.zh: 石廷柱之裔，本以散秩大臣世襲，至是，別授其兄祥泰散秩大臣。

translations.literal: Descendants of Shi Tingzhu had originally inherited the title of minister without specific duty; on this occasion his elder brother Xiangtai was separately granted minister without specific duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi family's minister-without-duty title went to his brother Xiangtai on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 回部平，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: When the Muslim regions were pacified his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After pacification his portrait entered the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 上追悼納穆札爾、三泰死事，為賦雙義詩，以傅清、拉布敦殉西藏，班第、鄂容安死伊犁相擬。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mourning the deaths of Namuzhal and San Tai, composed a poem on double righteousness, comparing them to Fu Qing and Labudun dying for Tibet and Bandi and E Rong'an dying at Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Namuzhal and San Tai, the Emperor wrote a "double righteousness" poem pairing them with Fu Qing and Labudun at Tibet and Bandi and E Rong'an at Ili.

sentences.zh: 謂「此六人者，事異心同，皆與國休戚之藎臣也」。

translations.literal: He said: "These six men encountered different circumstances, yet their hearts were the same—all were loyal ministers who shared fortune and misfortune with the state."
translations.idiomatic: He called all six "loyal ministers who shared the state's weal and woe," though their circumstances differed.

sentences.zh: 子佛柱，襲子爵、散秩大臣，官阿克蘇領隊大臣。

translations.literal: His son Fozhu inherited the viscounty and minister-without-duty title and served as Aksu detachment commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fozhu inherited the viscounty and served as Aksu detachment commander.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高宗朝徼外諸叛，霍集占最桀驁耐戰，方其困兆惠保葉爾羌，非師武臣力，幾不能克。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the Gaozong reign the rebellions beyond the frontier—Khoja Jahan was the most fierce and hard to fight; when he had trapped Zhaohui at Yarkand, had it not been for martial generals and ministers, victory would scarcely have been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator notes that among Gaozong's frontier rebels Khoja Jahan was fiercest—without martial ministers Zhaohui might never have escaped Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 阿睦爾撒納既叛，師未接，輒遠竄，非霍集占比也。

translations.literal: After Amursana rebelled, before troops engaged he fled far away—he cannot be compared with Khoja Jahan.
translations.idiomatic: Amursana fled before battle and cannot compare with Khoja Jahan.

sentences.zh: 珠爾默特那木札爾欲背中國，乃汗準噶爾，尤愚妄，殆不足數。

translations.literal: Dondrup Namjal wished to turn against China and hail the Dzungar khan was especially foolish and reckless, scarcely worth counting.
translations.idiomatic: Dondrup Namjal, who sought to betray China for a Dzungar khan, was too foolish to count.

sentences.zh: 六臣所遇異，故其效亦殊。

translations.literal: The six ministers met different circumstances, and therefore their effects also differed.
translations.idiomatic: The six ministers faced different tests and produced different outcomes.

sentences.zh: 大誅既加，罪人斯得，咸廩廩稱義烈矣。

translations.literal: Once great punishment had been applied and the guilty were obtained, all were reverently called martyrs of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after imperial punishment fell and guilt was settled, all were honored as righteous martyrs.
